topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer biology lecture series, outlines the intended learning outcomes, and welcomes students from various academic backgrounds.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological fundamentals of oncogenesis as an accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal tissue architecture and cellular differentiation programs.

topics.label: Mechanisms and pathology of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the histological and physical progression of tumors from localized, encapsulated growths to invasive malignancies capable of metastatic spread.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and pathophysiological impacts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how benign and malignant neoplasms are clinically categorized, named, and capable of causing morbidity and mortality through localized and systemic effects.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of cancer frequency and mortality across human populations and compare oncological occurrence throughout the animal kingdom.

topics.label: Clinical symptoms and cancer screening methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss early symptom presentation and evaluate clinical screening approaches used to detect pre-malignant lesions and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practicals preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the session by reiterating the learning outcomes and previewing the upcoming practicals and lectures.
